issues.label: Preliminary issue: scope of Commissioner's intervention
Issue 1: Proper factors for extension of time
Issue 2: Duty to provide adequate reasons
Issue 3: Whether extension of time constitutes impermissible collateral attack

result.overall: The judicial review application by the Attorney General of Canada challenging the Commissioner's decision to extend the time for Mr. Pentney to appeal was allowed, quashing the extension due to inadequate reasons and because the extension constituted an impermissible collateral attack on a final decision.

themes.name: Extension of time factors
themes.summary: The Court examined the proper factors and tests applicable to extending time for appeals under the CPP, including the Gattellaro four-part test and contextual factors specific to the Review Tribunal.

themes.name: Duty to provide adequate reasons
themes.summary: The Court considered whether the Commissioner had a duty to provide adequate reasons for extending time and found the reasons insufficient to support the exercise of discretion.

themes.name: Collateral attack and finality
themes.summary: The Court analyzed whether the extension of time constituted an impermissible collateral attack on a final decision of the Minister, relying on the Federal Court of Appeal's decision in Hogervorst and principles of finality.

arguments.quote: the Commissioner erred in law in failing to consider the relevant applicable factors governing the issue of when an extension of time to appeal may be granted under the CPP
arguments.claim: The Minister argued the Commissioner failed to consider the proper legal factors for extending time to appeal under the CPP.
arguments.outcome_note: Court found the Gattellaro factors relevant and the Commissioner applied a flexible approach.

arguments.quote: the Commissioner erred in failing to provide reasons for decision or adequate reasons for his grant of an extension of time
arguments.claim: The Minister argued the Commissioner breached the duty of fairness by not providing adequate reasons for extending time.
arguments.outcome_note: Court found reasons inadequate and intervention warranted.
arguments.gap: The Commissioner did not provide adequate reasons in the record to support the extension.

arguments.quote: the granting of an extension of time to appeal to the Review Tribunal the Minister’s first decision rendered in May 2003 was an impermissible collateral attack on the Minister’s February 6, 2006 decision
arguments.claim: The Minister argued the extension constituted an impermissible collateral attack on a final decision refusing reconsideration of a second application.
arguments.outcome_note: Court agreed the extension was a collateral attack and quashed the decision.

arguments.quote: the Commissioner adopted a principled approach to the exercise of his discretion on late appeal requests including the Gattellaro factors and contextual factors relevant to the Review Tribunal
arguments.claim: The Commissioner argued he applied the correct flexible and contextual approach to extending time, considering Gattellaro and additional factors specific to the Review Tribunal.
arguments.outcome_note: Court accepted the approach but found the reasons inadequate in this case.
arguments.quote_snapped: [28] In her memorandum of fact and law, counsel for the Commissioner wrote on this point at paragraph 38: The Commissioner has adopted a principled approach to the exercise of his discretion on late appeal requests that includes an assessment of the information available to him in the context of the factors identified in Canada (Minister of Human Resources Development) v.

arguments.quote: the Commissioner argued the law is well settled that a denial of a disability application by the Department will not prevent a person from being entitled to the disability benefit on a subsequent application
arguments.claim: The Commissioner argued that multiple applications are allowed and res judicata does not apply to Minister's administrative decisions.
arguments.outcome_note: Court found the extension was a collateral attack inconsistent with finality principles.
arguments.quote_snapped: [77] Counsel for the Commissioner argues the law is well settled that a denial of a disability application by the Department, providing there is no appeal to a Review Tribunal, will not prevent a person from being entitled to the disability benefit on a subsequent application.

holdings.quote: The functional and pragmatic analysis points to the standard of review of correctness
holdings.statement: The Court held that the standard of review for the Commissioner's legal discretion to extend time is correctness.

holdings.quote: the standard four-prong test is relevant to all instances in which an extension of time to commence a proceeding is at stake
holdings.statement: The Court held the Gattellaro four-part test is relevant and not exclusive for extension of time decisions, allowing flexibility and contextual factors.
holdings.quote_snapped: [42] As I see it, the essence of the jurisprudence is that the standard four part test is relevant to all instances in which an extension of time to commence a proceeding is at stake whether it be the commencement of a proceeding in this Court or before an administrative tribunal.

holdings.quote: the Commissioner had an obligation to provide reasons for extending the time to appeal to the Review Tribunal
holdings.statement: The Court concluded the Commissioner must provide reasons for extending time, especially given the length of delay.

holdings.quote: the record before me fails to disclose adequate reasons for the grant of an extension of time and this failure warrants this Court’s intervention
holdings.statement: The Court found the reasons given were inadequate and justified judicial intervention to quash the extension.

holdings.quote: the extension of time in this case constitutes an impermissible collateral attack on a previous final decision of the Minister
holdings.statement: The Court held the extension constituted an impermissible collateral attack on a final decision and quashed the Commissioner's decision.

holdings.quote: this judicial review application is allowed. The Commissioner’s decision to extend time to appeal to the Review Tribunal the Minister’s May 28, 2003 decision is quashed
holdings.statement: The Court allowed the judicial review and quashed the Commissioner's extension of time decision.

rebuttals.quote: the Commissioner’s intervention went beyond the scope of the limited intervention granted by Prothonotory Tabib
rebuttals.point: The Commissioner improperly argued against the Minister on collateral attack and reasons issues
rebuttals.court_answer: The Court agreed with the Minister and resolved the matter by having Mr. Pentney adopt the Commissioner’s submissions.

authorities.quote: the correct legal test is on a motion for an extension of time to file an application for leave to appeal: see Marshall v. Canada, 2002 FCA 172; Neis v. Baksa, 2002 FCA 230
authorities.authority: Marshall v. Canada; Neis v. Baksa
authorities.why: These cases set out the four-part test for extension of time which the Court applied.

authorities.quote: the underlying consideration in an application to extend time is to ensure that justice is done between the parties: Grewal v. Canada (Min. of Employment and Immigration), [1985] 2 F.C. 263
authorities.why: The Court recognized the flexible and justice-oriented nature of the extension of time test.
authorities.quote_snapped: 263 that the underlying consideration in an application to extend time is to ensure that justice is done between the parties.

authorities.quote: the principle against collateral attacks and the principle of finality of an administrative decision have been breached affecting the integrity of the scheme mandated by the CPP: Hogervorst, 2007 FCA 41
authorities.authority: Minister of Human Resources Development v. Hogervorst
authorities.why: The Court relied on Hogervorst to hold that the extension was an impermissible collateral attack and violated finality.
authorities.quote_snapped: [88] On the facts of this case, I would hold that both the principle against collateral attacks and the principle of finality of an administrative decision have been breached affecting the integrity of the scheme mandated by the CPP.

authorities.quote: the duty of procedural fairness will require the provision of a written explanation for a decision: Baker v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), [1999] 2 S.C.R. 817
authorities.why: The Court applied Baker to require reasons for the extension decision.
authorities.quote_snapped: 817 at paragraphs 35 through 44 where Justice L’Heureux-Dubé (on behalf of the Supreme Court of Canada), discussed the requirements emphasizing that at paragraph 43 where she wrote: 43 In my opinion, it is now appropriate to recognize that, in certain circumstances, the duty of procedural fairness will require the provision of a written explanation for a decision.
